sentences.text: Revenue has cycled rather than compounded: it peaked at $236 billion in FY2022 [F7], then fell three years running to $184 billion in FY2025 [F10], a three-year CAGR of -7.9% [D626].
The 5.4% revenue CAGR over the full window [F177] mixes presentations, because FY2018 and FY2021 to FY2025 are later recasts of the first-reported figures [F3][X3][F7][X7].
Revenue rose 51.5% in FY2022 [D232] and net income rose 127.6% [D233]; the filing attributes the pre-tax gain to higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57].
FY2020 was the weakest year, with revenue down 32.5% [D153] and a net margin of -5.9% [D611]; the filings cited do not explain that year.
In FY2025 Chevron U.S.A. Inc. was 75.1% of revenue [D402], fell 5.3% [D403] and took 3.9pp off the 4.6% total decline [D404][D358].
Operating Segments — US, Upstream grew 34.0% [D553], added 2.5pp [D554], the largest positive contribution, and reached 10.6% of revenue [D552].
Revenue fell 4.6% [D358] to $184 billion [F10]; the filing attributes this mainly to lower crude and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes and gas prices [P17].
Operating costs fell 3.4% [D373] against revenue's 4.6% decline [D358], so revenue growth minus cost growth was -1.2pp [D379], negative operating leverage.
Diluted EPS fell 31.8% [D361], more than net income's 30.5% [D359], because diluted shares rose 2.1% [D374].
The FY2025 net margin of 6.7% [F30] is below the 7.9% window median [D613] and the 10.2% energy peer median [D632], ranking 33rd percentile of six peers [D631].
Cost of revenue fell 9.2% [D370], taking its share of revenue to 57.2% from 58.8% [D338][D296], a 1.6pp gain, as purchased crude and products fell [P14].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% [D345] from 27.6% [D261] in FY2023, which the filing attributes to the mix of earnings across tax jurisdictions [P33].
DD&A rose to 10.7% of revenue [D341] from 8.5% [D299], which the filing attributes to higher production and rates [P12].
The largest window move was FY2021's +15.9pp net margin gain [D201]; the filings cited do not explain it.
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion [F60] was 2.76x net income [D346], and free cash flow was 1.35x [D347] against a 1.10x window median [D622].
Free cash flow margin was 8.8% [D343], just below its 8.9% window median [D616], while capex took 9.2% of revenue [D342].
The filing guides 2026 organic capex to $18 to $19 billion [P4], above FY2025's $17.3 billion [F70], which was 0.86x D&A [D348].
Operating cash flow rose 7.8% [D362] in FY2025, which the filing attributes to higher TCO distributions and legacy Hess contributions that offset lower prices [P6].
Net cash was $3.96 billion [D351], or 2.1% of revenue [D352], up from -$156 million [D309] in FY2024.
That ranks at the 83rd percentile among six energy peers [D637], against a peer median of -7.7% of revenue [D638].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $24.8 billion [D353], or 149.7% of free cash flow [D354].
Diluted shares still rose 2.1% [D374], and the filings cited do not explain why.
Revenue has fallen three years running, down 16.5% [D274], 1.8% [D316] and 4.6% [D358] from FY2023 to FY2025 [R1]; the FY2025 cut reflects lower prices [P17].
Net income fell 39.7% [D275], 17.3% [D317] and 30.5% [D359] over the same years, a CAGR of -29.8% [D627] against revenue's -7.9% [D626].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 to FY2025, at 132.8% [D270], 179.7% [D312] and 149.7% [D354] [R4]; asset sales of about $9 billion since 2024 were a partial offset [P31].
FY2018 and FY2021 to FY2025 are later revenue recasts, so growth in those years mixes presentations; first-reported growth was 17.4% [D629] and 71.6% [D630] [R3].
In the FY2026 10-K, a net margin above the 7.9% window median [D613] would reverse the decline from 6.7% [F30]; a reading below 6.7% [F30] would confirm it.
In the FY2026 10-K, buybacks and dividends falling below the FY2023 level of 132.8% of free cash flow [D270] would show a return toward self-funding; a rise above 149.7% [D354] would widen the gap.
In the FY2026 10-K, capex above the FY2024 level of 0.95x D&A [D306], against the 0.86x of FY2025 [D348] and the $18 to $19 billion guidance [P4], would confirm a higher investment load.
